description: No schedule: the CronJob in platform/renovate is the schedule, and every run may open PRs. Default prHourlyLimit of 2 starves the queue, so majors (sorted last) never win a slot. prConcurrentLimit is uncapped because updates are grouped per app directory, which already bounds open PRs at roughly one per app.

packageRules.description: linuxserver images pull from lscr.io but are tracked through a # renovate: comment naming their ghcr.io twin. helm-values also extracts the lscr.io repository, a second lookup of the same tags that ends on ghcr.io's rate limit anyway.
These images are tracked by GitHub release, which upstream publishes before the image is pushed. Waiting keeps a PR from pointing at a tag that does not exist yet.
One PR per app directory, so a chart bump and the image bump it pairs with land together. This also keeps Nextcloud, which cannot skip majors, out of any batch.

Patches merge on their own once the validate check passes. A group automerges only if every update in it does, so a chart patch paired with an image minor still waits for review. Rules below this one opt specific deps back out. A release with no timestamp skips the wait instead of never opening.

linuxserver restarted sonarr's build counter at ls1 after ls329, so the stale ls325-ls329 builds sort as newer than the current one. Regex versioning counts an ls bump as a patch, so without this the old build would automerge. Drop this once sonarr moves past 4.0.20.3014.
bootstrap/ releases are applied by hand with just bootstrap-*, so an automerge would only move git away from what is running.
Longhorn upgrades are an ordered procedure with version-specific notes per release, not a chart to bump on sight. dependencyDashboardApproval means no PR opens until it is ticked.

A k3s minor bump has to wait for Cilium to support that Kubernetes minor, so without this every patch release sits behind a minor PR that can't merge yet. Even a patch means rolling every node, so none of them automerge.
